catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 10 - BLIND FIRST READING (unverified image reading)

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of the work, author, or any earlier reading of these fragments. This is a blind reading.

Method note: Besides viewing all 16 supplied images with the Read tool, I made enlarged (2x), contrast-enhanced, greyscale copies of each native-resolution tile (each split into three overlapping horizontal bands) in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-aaymeloglu--claude-assistant/c674cb30-f1b2-4f00-9935-8959914c1fa4/scratchpad/work/zoom10/ (files z002_0.png ... z016_2.png). I read from those copies as well as the originals. Before listing the images I ran a short Python command inside the packet directory to print their filenames and sizes (filename glob image-*.jpg only; packet.json not opened). Nothing else was opened. All 16 images loaded. None failed.

======================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (observations only)
======================================================================

The packet shows two parchment strips, each photographed on both sides with a 17 cm ruler. The strips carry the labels "A" and "B".

- image-001: strip A, one side. The strip is about 3.8 cm wide and about 15 cm high. It holds one narrow column of about 37-38 lines of small Gothic cursive/bookhand in brown ink. The text runs off the LEFT edge, where words are cut, and the right edge of the writing looks close to complete. There is a blank lower margin with holes and nicks, which look like sewing or binding holes or cuts. There is a dark ink blot near line 3.
- image-005: strip A, the other side. The text runs off the RIGHT edge (words cut), and a blank strip lies at the left. A darker band or overlap at the top and bottom suggests the strip was folded or pasted. About 37 lines.
- image-009: strip B, one side. The text runs off the right edge. About 39 lines.
- image-013: strip B, the other side. The text starts at the left with initial letters sometimes clipped and runs to near the right edge. About 37 lines.
- Tiles: 002-004 (A, side of 001), 006-008 (A, side of 005), 010-012 (B, side of 009), 014-016 (B, side of 013). Successive tiles overlap by several lines.

Visible features:
- There are no running titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, or coloured ink that I could see. All the writing appears to be in one brown ink.
- There is no underlining that I could confirm.
- Interlinear additions occur. They are small letters or syllables written above words, e.g. "eu"/"en" above line 2 of image-002, "do" above a word in image-003, and "ne" above line-ends in image-003. Some may be abbreviation-completion letters rather than corrections.
- I saw no marginal glosses. There is a small mark ("a"? with a curved stroke) in the left blank margin of image-007, about lines 4-5. It may be a signe de renvoi, a stray mark, or a letter. I cannot tell.
- Frequent short citation-like tokens appear: "Jo.", "Ro. vi.", "apo. viii.", "Tren. i.", "Jo. xi.?". They are followed by roman numerals, and to me they look like abbreviated book-and-chapter references embedded in running prose. That is an interpretation of form only.
- The text is a single continuous prose column on each side. Each strip is a vertical cut from a larger leaf, so the full width of the original column is not preserved. I cannot tell from these crops whether the leaf had one column or two.

======================================================================
2. SELECTION
======================================================================

I attempted a line-by-line reading of every side, concentrating on:
- strip A side 1 (tiles 002-004), the clearest side;
- strip B side 2 (tiles 014-016), also comparatively clear;
- citation-bearing lines on all sides.

Strip A side 2 (006-008) and strip B side 1 (010-012) are fainter and more abraded. I give partial readings there.

The texts are cut on one side throughout, so no line is complete. Where I give no reading, the line is unread or illegible.

Overlaps: Lines repeated across adjacent tiles are noted as "= image-NNN line n" and are not new text.

Conventions: (xx) is an expansion. "word?" marks an uncertain reading. [illegible] marks unread text. "|" is the physical cut edge where it matters. Abbreviation signs are described in words where I could not render them: "p-bar" = p with a stroke through the descender, "sup." = a superscript letter.

======================================================================
3. TRANSCRIPTION
======================================================================
